issues.explanation: The action sets status, called_at and called_by_user_id by hand instead of reusing Ticket::call(), duplicating the write-once transition and any guards or events that method owns.
The test claims a normal_only call resets the streak, but the normal is called through the default Any mode, so NormalOnly/PriorityOnly ignoring the fairness rule after a streak is never exercised.
waiting() and called() are declared in the global namespace; Pest includes all test files in one process, so another test file using those generic names would cause a redeclaration fatal error.
The Ticket::retrieved listener is registered globally and never removed, leaking test state into later tests in the same process (currently masked only by the $raced flag).

review.summary: Adds the CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException and an invokable CallNextTicket action implementing deterministic ordering, per-mode selection, the 3-priority-call fairness rule, inactive-queue rejection, lock-based exactly-once semantics, docs/CHANGELOG and a broad Pest suite. The core logic matches the task; the remaining feedback is minor (reuse Ticket::call(), close the fairness-ignored test gap, tidy test globals), so this is an approve-with-nits. Confidence is medium because the diff does not show the existing Ticket, TicketStatus, TicketFactory and InactiveQueueException definitions that the action and tests rely on.
